 By : CNBCTV18.com November 2, 2026 | 07:13 IST Edited by Priyanka Deshpande 
 Published On Nov 2, 2026 | 05:00 IST 
 Last Updated On Nov 2, 2026 | 07:13 IST

 Summary Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu are among the regions likely to receive heavy rainfall, while Odisha and Chhattisgarh may also see intense rain over the coming days. Delhi is expected to have mainly clear skies on November 2.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source Cyclonic Storm Murasu has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal.
 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it was expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between late November 2 and the early hours of November 3.
 In its latest bulletin, the IMD said the storm had moved north-westwards at 20 kmph over the previous six hours and was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 2.30 am IST on November 2.
 The IMD expects Murasu to continue moving north-westwards and cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, as a severe cyclonic storm. It forecast sustained wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph, during landfall between 11.30 pm on November 2 and 4 am on November 3.
 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast extremely heavy rainfall in Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam, as well as parts of Telangana, with the storm expected to make landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast around midnight on November 2.
 Andhra Pradesh: Heavy rain, strong winds expected 
 Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on November 2, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and gusty winds reaching 80-90 kmph.
 The IMD has forecast that the cyclone will cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, bringing winds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts are likely to experience the highest storm surge, which could reach about 1 metre above the astronomical tide and inundate low-lying areas.
 Rayalaseema is also likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on November 2, with gusty winds and thundersqualls in some areas.
 Telangana: Heavy to very heavy rain likely 
 Telangana is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on November 2, with isolated very heavy rainfall forecast in some areas.
 The IMD has also warned of thunderstorms and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph. Squally winds are expected to begin from the afternoon, with speeds likely to increase overnight.
 The rainfall activity is expected to intensify further on November 3, when isolated extremely heavy rainfall is also forecast.
 Tamil Nadu: Heavy rain in several areas 
 Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to receive isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall on November 2. The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph.
 Strong winds are expected along and off the north Tamil Nadu-Puducherry coast, with speeds likely to reach 55-65 kmph, gusting to 75 kmph, on November 2 morning. These could increase to 60-70 kmph, with gusts up to 80 kmph, by evening.
 Karnataka: Rainfall likely in coastal and interior districts 
 Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on November 2. Isolated heavy rainfall is forecast over South Interior Karnataka, while North Interior Karnataka is likely to see isolated to scattered rainfall.
 The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms and gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, over parts of the state.
 Kerala: Rain and gusty winds forecast 
 Kerala and Mahe are likely to receive isolated heavy rainfall on November 2. The IMD has forecast fairly widespread to widespread rainfall across the region during the November 1-7 period.
 Gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, are also likely.
 Odisha: Rainfall activity to increase 
 Odisha is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on November 2, with fairly widespread to widespread rainfall expected across the state. Isolated heavy rainfall is also forecast, along with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph.
 Rainfall is expected to intensify over south Odisha on November 3 and 4, when isolated very heavy rainfall is forecast.
 Weather forecast across other regions on November 2 
 North India: Delhi is likely to witness mainly clear skies, with maximum and minimum temperatures ranging between 28°C and 30°C and 16°C and 18°C, respectively. East Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall, while shallow to moderate fog is forecast at isolated places. Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand may also receive isolated rainfall.
 Central India: Isolated to scattered rainfall is likely over East Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha and parts of Chhattisgarh. Chhattisgarh may also receive isolated heavy rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning.
 East India: Odisha is likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall, with isolated heavy rainfall in some areas. Jharkhand, Bihar, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim, and Gangetic West Bengal may receive isolated to scattered rainfall.
 Northeast India: Arunachal Pradesh is likely to receive isolated heavy rainfall. Isolated to scattered rainfall is also forecast over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura.
 West India: Isolated to scattered rainfall is likely over Konkan and Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada and Gujarat Region. Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also likely over parts of Maharashtra.
 IMD issues fishermen warning, advises caution 
 The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the southeast, southwest and west-central Bay of Bengal on November 2. Fishing activities have also been restricted along and off the Andhra Pradesh coast, as well as the north Tamil Nadu-Puducherry coast, due to strong winds and rough sea conditions.
 The weather agency has warned that heavy rainfall and strong winds could damage vulnerable structures, disrupt road and rail traffic, cause waterlogging and flooding in low-lying areas, and affect small boats and fishing vessels.
 People in vulnerable areas have been advised to monitor weather updates, move to safer locations if required and avoid taking shelter under trees during thunderstorms.
